description: The classical core of artificial intelligence: search, constraint satisfaction, adversarial games, logic and inference, decision theory, Markov decision processes, and the entry points to machine learning, neural networks and bio-inspired methods, each implemented and run on real problems. Taught to the depth of the standard introductory AI course.
modelledOn: Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
Poole and Mackworth, Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (introductory chapters)
outcomes: Formulate problems as state spaces and solve them with uninformed and informed search, including A* with admissible heuristics.
Model and solve constraint satisfaction problems with backtracking, propagation and local search.
Play adversarial games with minimax, alpha-beta pruning and expectimax.
Represent knowledge in propositional and first-order logic and perform inference by resolution and chaining.
Make decisions under uncertainty with Bayesian networks, utility theory and Markov decision processes.
Train simple classifiers, perceptrons and neural networks and apply genetic algorithms and swarm methods.

units.title: Introduction to AI and intelligent agents
topics: What AI is: history from Turing to deep learning and large language models; the Turing test and its critics
Agents, environments, rationality; PEAS descriptions; agent types
AI in Africa: crop disease detection, language technology for Twi and Hausa, mobile-money fraud detection
Setting up Python with NumPy and a search/game framework

units.title: Search and planning
topics: Problem formulation: states, actions, transition model, goal test, path cost; 8-puzzle, route finding in Accra
Uninformed search: BFS, DFS, uniform cost, depth-limited, iterative deepening, bidirectional; completeness and complexity
Informed search: greedy best-first, A*, admissible and consistent heuristics, heuristic design, IDA*
Local search: hill climbing, simulated annealing, beam search; continuous spaces
Classical planning: STRIPS representation, forward and backward state-space planning, planning graphs
Searching with nondeterminism and partial observability in brief

units.title: Constraint satisfaction problems
topics: Variables, domains, constraints; map colouring, timetabling, sudoku, N-queens
Backtracking search with variable and value ordering (MRV, degree, least constraining value)
Inference: forward checking, arc consistency (AC-3), constraint propagation
Local search for CSPs (min-conflicts); problem structure and tree decomposition

units.title: Game trees and tree-structured computation
topics: Games as search: minimax, optimal play, evaluation functions and cut-offs
Alpha-beta pruning and move ordering; transposition tables
Stochastic games and expectimax; Monte Carlo tree search
Building an Oware or tic-tac-toe player and measuring its strength

units.title: Propositional and first-order logic, inference
topics: Knowledge-based agents; propositional logic: syntax, semantics, entailment, model checking
Inference: resolution, conjunctive normal form, forward and backward chaining with Horn clauses; SAT solvers (DPLL, WalkSAT)
First-order logic: syntax, semantics, quantifiers, knowledge engineering
Inference in first-order logic: unification, forward and backward chaining, resolution; Prolog
Knowledge representation: ontologies, semantic networks, frames, the open-world problem

units.title: Uncertainty and decision theory
topics: Probability review; Bayes' rule and naive Bayes
Bayesian networks: representation, conditional independence, exact inference by enumeration and variable elimination, sampling
Utility theory, expected utility, decision networks, value of information
A medical diagnosis or crop advisory decision network

units.title: Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning
topics: MDPs: states, actions, rewards, discounting, policies; Bellman equations
Value iteration and policy iteration
Reinforcement learning: passive and active, temporal-difference learning, Q-learning, exploration versus exploitation
Grid-world and a simple inventory-control agent

units.title: Introduction to machine learning
topics: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning; training, validation, test sets; overfitting
Concept learning: hypothesis spaces, version spaces, decision trees (ID3, information gain)
k-nearest neighbours, linear and logistic regression, naive Bayes; evaluation metrics
Clustering with k-means

units.title: Artificial neural networks
topics: The perceptron and its learning rule; linear separability
Multilayer networks, activation functions, backpropagation, gradient descent
Training a small network on handwritten digits; introduction to convolutional networks
Where deep learning and large language models fit; limits and risks

units.title: Bio-inspired algorithms and AI ethics
topics: Genetic algorithms: representation, selection, crossover, mutation; solving a timetabling problem
Swarm intelligence: ant colony optimisation, particle swarm optimisation
Artificial immune systems and cellular automata in brief
Ethics and society: bias, fairness, explainability, safety, jobs, AI policy in Ghana and the AU

schedule.title: What AI is: agents and environments
schedule.exercise: Write a PEAS description and agent-type classification for a crop-disease detection app used by farmers in northern Ghana, then argue in half a page whether it passes any useful version of the Turing test.

tasks.title: Set up Python with NumPy, run a provided script that prints a 3x3 grid state, and confirm the printed array matches the expected output
Code a simple reflex vacuum agent for a two-room world and record its performance measure over 20 steps from each starting state
Compare a reflex agent and a model-based agent in a partially observable grid with random dirt, and report which scores higher over 100 runs

schedule.title: Problem formulation and uninformed search
schedule.exercise: Formulate a delivery route between five Accra locations as a search problem (states, actions, costs, goal test) and hand-trace BFS and uniform-cost search on it, showing frontier contents at each step.

tasks.title: Run breadth-first search on a given 8-puzzle start state in the visualiser and record the order of the first 10 expanded nodes
Compare DFS, iterative deepening and uniform-cost search on a weighted route graph and tabulate nodes expanded and path cost for each
Formulate a new sliding-tile variant with a custom goal state, then show which uninformed method solves it within a 5000-node budget

schedule.title: Informed and local search
schedule.exercise: Prove that Manhattan distance is admissible for the 8-puzzle, then design and justify a second heuristic and argue whether it dominates the first.

tasks.title: Step through A* on a small grid map with the Manhattan heuristic and list f, g and h values for the first eight expanded nodes
Run A* on 5 random 8-puzzle instances with misplaced-tiles and Manhattan heuristics and compare nodes expanded to show which dominates
Implement simulated annealing for an 8-queens board, tune the cooling schedule, and report success rate over 50 random starts versus plain hill climbing

schedule.title: Planning and uncertain environments
schedule.exercise: Write STRIPS actions and a goal for a mobile-money agent delivering cash to a customer, then produce a forward-search plan by hand and note where partial observability would break it.

tasks.title: Use the visualiser to forward-search a three-block blocks-world STRIPS problem and write out the resulting four-step plan with each action's preconditions
Code a breadth-first STRIPS planner for a blocks-world with four blocks and verify its plan reaches the goal from a given start state
Build a belief-state search for a sensorless vacuum agent in a three-room world and show a conformant plan that reaches a clean state

schedule.title: Constraint satisfaction problems
schedule.exercise: Model a weekly exam timetable for four courses and three rooms as a CSP, list variables, domains and constraints, and solve it by hand with MRV and forward checking.

tasks.title: Encode the Australia-style map colouring problem with three colours as a CSP in Python and check a hand-found solution satisfies every constraint
Implement AC-3 on a 4x4 sudoku-like CSP and report which domains shrink before any backtracking begins
Compare plain backtracking, MRV with forward checking, and min-conflicts on N-queens for N from 8 to 40, reporting runtime for each

schedule.title: Game trees and adversarial search
schedule.exercise: Compute minimax values by hand for a given three-ply game tree, mark the branches alpha-beta prunes, and explain how move ordering changes the count of pruned nodes.

tasks.title: Run minimax on a provided two-ply tic-tac-toe tree in the visualiser and write the backed-up value at each node
Run alpha-beta on a given depth-4 tree with good and bad move ordering and compare the number of leaves evaluated in each case
Build an Oware player with depth-limited alpha-beta and a custom evaluation function, then measure its win rate against a random player over 100 games

schedule.title: Propositional and first-order logic
schedule.exercise: Encode a small rule base for deciding whether a market trader qualifies for a microloan as propositional Horn clauses, convert one rule to CNF, and prove a query by resolution.

tasks.title: Build a truth table for three propositional sentences and decide by model checking whether the first entails the third
Run forward and backward chaining on a ten-rule Horn knowledge base and compare which facts each method derives for the query
Implement DPLL and test it on 20 random 3-SAT instances with ratios near 4.3 clauses per variable, plotting solve time against ratio

schedule.title: First-order inference and knowledge representation
schedule.exercise: Draw a semantic network for a small Ghanaian family-and-clan domain, then write five Prolog-style rules for relations such as uncle and cousin and trace one query by unification.

tasks.title: Unify five given pairs of first-order terms in the rules tool and record the substitution or the failure reason for each pair
Run backward chaining on a family-relations rule base and trace the proof tree for the query grandparent(kofi, X)
Extend a given animal ontology with three new classes and rules, and show a query that fails under closed-world but succeeds under open-world reading

schedule.title: Probability, Bayesian networks and decisions
schedule.exercise: Build a small Bayesian network for malaria diagnosis from fever, rapid-test result and rainy season, compute a posterior by enumeration, and decide whether to treat using expected utility.

tasks.title: Apply Bayes rule to a rapid malaria test with given sensitivity and prevalence and compute the posterior probability of disease after a positive result
Code inference by enumeration for a five-node Bayesian network and verify two posteriors against hand calculation within 0.001
Build a crop advisory decision network with rainfall forecast and compute the value of perfect information for a planting decision under given costs

schedule.title: Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning
schedule.exercise: Write the MDP for a small shop deciding weekly stock levels, state the Bellman equation for it, and perform two sweeps of value iteration by hand.

tasks.title: Run value iteration on a 4x3 grid-world and record the utility of each cell after iterations 1, 2 and convergence
Implement tabular Q-learning on a grid-world with a pit and goal and plot episode return over 500 episodes
Train a Q-learning inventory agent with random demand and compare its average profit against a fixed reorder-point policy over 200 simulated weeks

schedule.title: Introduction to machine learning
schedule.exercise: Given a small table of 14 farm records, compute information gain by hand for two attributes, choose the root of an ID3 tree, and discuss how overfitting would show up on new records.

tasks.title: Build an ID3 decision tree on the provided play-or-not dataset in the visualiser and record the information gain at the root split
Train k-nearest neighbours and logistic regression on a provided dataset, report accuracy, precision and recall on a held-out test split, and compare
Implement k-means from scratch, choose k using the elbow method on a customer dataset, and show how three random initialisations change the result

schedule.title: Artificial neural networks
schedule.exercise: Explain in one page why a single perceptron cannot learn XOR, show a two-layer network that can, and note two risks of deploying a large language model in a Ghanaian clinic.

tasks.title: Train a perceptron on the AND and OR datasets in the visualiser and record the weights after each epoch until convergence
Train a two-hidden-unit network on XOR with sigmoid activations and watch the loss curve to find a learning rate that converges in under 2000 epochs
Train a small network on a handwritten digits subset, report test accuracy, and diagnose overfitting by comparing training and validation curves

schedule.title: Bio-inspired algorithms and AI ethics
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page policy brief on bias and fairness in a mobile-money fraud detector, referring to current Ghanaian and African Union AI policy directions, with two concrete safeguards.

tasks.title: Run Conway's Game of Life on a glider and a blinker in the visualiser and record the pattern after 4 generations
Implement a genetic algorithm that solves a small class timetable with 6 courses and 4 slots, and plot best fitness per generation
Apply ant colony optimisation to a 12-town travelling salesman instance and compare tour length with a nearest-neighbour baseline over 20 runs
